messages:
alex: quick heads-up, I did a reranker+embed throughput sweep across eu-west1 / us-central1 / ap-southeast1 this morning. testing dims [256, 768, 1536], batch sizes [1,8,32,128], cpu vs gpu, int8 vs fp16. attaching raw numbers below and a few highlights. can folks eyeball for weird region artifacts?

benchbot: automated summary uploaded: https://dashboards.internal/reports/1923456789 (csv + charts). p50/p95/qps per-region per-config. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maria: nice. did you run int8 as per-channel quant or dynamic? which kernel flags for attention?

alex: per-channel int8 for the runs by default. kernel was the newer triton_fast_attention on GPUs, fallback to avx512 kernels on cpu. results: int8 ~1.6-1.9x throughput uplift on GPU for dims >=768, smaller uplift for 256. quality: small BLANC/rr drop ~0.9-1.5 points at 1536 dims on int8-perchannel.

ryan: curious — ap-southeast1 CPU numbers look surprisingly close to gpus for dim=256 @ batch=32 (cpu ~900 qps vs gpu ~1200 qps). what instance types? sounds like we might be saturating memcopy/PCIe more than compute for that workload.

anna: we were using c6i.large-ish for cpu runs (2x vCPU), and g4dn.xlarge for gpu. also forgot to enable NUMA pinning on the cpu run in apac for one of the early jobs — p95 inflated there by ~30ms in logs.

alex: good catch. I re-ran the cpu 256/32 with numa pinning enabled, p95 dropped ~28ms and qps improved ~12%. original run log snippet:```
[2026-03-12 09:02:11] runner: starting job dims=256 batch=32 node=ap-southeast1-c6i numa=off
[2026-03-12 09:02:43] runner: p50=21ms p95=143ms qps=780
```
re-run:```
[2026-03-12 09:33:02] runner: numa=on p50=19ms p95=115ms qps=870
```

maria: thanks. for the gpu kernel choices, did you compare triton_fast_attention vs flash-attn? any stability differences?

alex: yes — flash-attn slightly better latency for larger dims at batch=1 (p50 down ~6-8ms) but triton_fast gave better aggregate throughput at higher batch sizes (32/128) due to better batching paths and fewer kernel launches. also flash-attn had 1-2% higher tail variance in eu-west1 on the 80GB GPUs (probably driver/kernel mismatch).

ryan: behaving as expected. cost tradeoffs? if we route small dim requests to cpu and larger dims to gpu, what's the rough cost delta?

benchbot: quick cost calc (approx per 1M requests, from the run configs):
- route-all-gpu: $1,950
- cpu-for-dim<=256, gpu-else: $1,280 (savings ~34%)
- mixed with int8 on gpu: $1,070 (savings ~45%)
note: assumes our reserved instance rates in eu-west1 and does not include networking egress.

anna: suggest adding a routing rule in the proxy: if dims<=256 and batch>=8 -> prefer cpu pool, else gpu. fallback: if gpu int8 latency regress >2x then route to fp16 variant.

maria: can we make the fallback automated? e.g., quick eval on sample set comparing recent baseline and int8, trigger route if quality delta > 1.0 on rerank metric.

alex: yes, Redwood routing supports policy-based rollouts. plan: canary int8 in eu-west1 at 5% traffic, auto-eval on prompt-set A (1000 queries) every 30m, rollback if rerank-metric drop >1.0 or p95 degrade >20%. I'll open the rollout PR.

ryan: add one more item: ensure model variant labeling includes kernel and quant tags (e.g., v1-int8-triton). otherwise proxy can't pick correct fallback.

alex: will do. PR + canary scheduled for tomorrow 10:00 UTC. thanks for the checks. :thumbsup:

maria: nice work — any weird region-specific oddities left?

alex: only one remaining: us-central1 had intermittent 5-7% p95 spikes on fp16 large-batch runs coincident with scheduled maintenance window on node pool. re-ran outside window and spikes disappeared. I'll mark that run noisy in the CSV.

benchbot: noted noisy runs: 1923456789-run-03, 1923456789-run-11. CSV updated.

anna: cool. let me know when the canary PR is up, I'll validate the eval harness and add the swap rule for small dims.

alex: will ping here when PR is ready.
